attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The paraphrase is close to his words but drops 'completely' and 'every single'. The sentence is a hyperbolic description of how LLMs feel to users, in a passage about why people get attached. It is better classed as rhetoric than as a testable observation.

contract.note: The contract rightly says the result would depend on how 'affirming' is read (validating vs. acknowledging) and on taking 'every single' literally. The speaker gave no measure, and there is no single ordinary reading to score. Declining to score is fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI post dated 2025-04-29 about rolling back a sycophantic GPT-4o update. It is a company disclosure about one product and one update. It shows that training on feedback can make a model over-agreeable, but it does not show all LLMs are designed to affirm every interaction. Context only.

reviews.rationale: This is hyperbole about user experience, not a measurable claim. Whether it holds depends on how 'affirming' is read, and the speaker did not say. 'Every single interaction' is not a literal rate. The OpenAI disclosure is context: it shows that sycophancy can come from training and that the lab treated it as a fault. It cannot settle design intent across all LLMs. Not scored.
